thread:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: PAGERS: spike of 5xx from ALB(ingress-eu-west-2) showing surge in connection resets across AZ-b and AZ-c. Threshold hit: 500 error rate > 8% for 3m. Paging escalation to oncall.
eng-oncall: ACK. I'm on it — grabbing metrics and logs now. Anyone on netops?
maria g.: I'm awake, stepping in. Can we confirm whether it's ALB or Envoy at the edge? Cloud provider metric shows `TargetResponseTime` up too.
leo k.: seeing Envoy upstream 503/502 counters climbing on ingress pods in eu-west-2a/b. ctl logs show repeated `connection reset by peer` from upstream.
chris t.: FYI we had a small rollout to the model-serving autoscaler earlier but that was in eu-west-1 only. Not related afaict.
eng-oncall: running quick check: `kubectl -n ingress get pods -l app=ingress -o wide` -> some pods in eu-west-2b at 1/2 readiness.
eng-oncall: inspecting envoy stats: `curl -s http://ingress-service/stats | grep reset` -> lots of `downstream_cx_reset` and `upstream_cx_reset` spikes.
maria g.: timeline: ~06:12 UTC first spike, sustained at 06:16. Route53 health checks show intermittent failures for eu-west-2 ALBs.
netops-bot: Noted: AWS reports degraded packet loss in eu-west-2 AZ-b (SNS alert). Opening a ticket with provider: INC-100421.
eng-oncall: Core mitigation plan: 1) divert traffic off problematic AZs via weighted DNS 2) cordon/evict bad ingress nodes 3) scale ingress replicas and restart envoy 4) if ALB target instability persists, move to NLB fallback for critical routes.
ashley p.: Customer-impact check: CS reports elevated product errors for customers in EU region—some timeouts and 5xx complaints. Pulling list of impacted customers.
customer-success: We have at least 3 paying customers reporting visible errors; flagging as P2 customer-impacting incident. They want ETA.
leo k.: quick test from inside cluster: tcpdump shows TLS handshakes completing then RST from target IPs after ~100ms. Looks like backend instances are dropping connections under load.
maria g.: Can we check connection tracking on nodes? `sudo ss -s` shows many TIME-WAIT but not exhaustion. However, `conntrack -S` shows spikes approaching high-water on AZ-b.
eng-oncall: Running `kubectl drain` of node eu-west-2b-ingress-3 (cordon + evict) as a soft mitigation to reduce resets. Will monitor.
eng-oncall: `kubectl drain eu-west-2b-ingress-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` -> eviction in progress.
leo k.: After cordon, upstream reset rate dropped ~30% on that node. But still high overall because multiple nodes affected.
netops-bot: AWS: Assigned ENGENG ticket INC-100421 to network team. Provider indicates transient fabric issue between AZ-b and AKS target group.
maria g.: Let's immediately shift Route53 weights: reduce eu-west-2 AZ-b and AZ-c to 0, route traffic to eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 for the next 30m. Who can make the DNS change?
ashley p.: I can action that. Making weighted-routing change now -> updating weights in console.
ashley p.: Done. Route53 records updated, prepropagation TTL 60s. Will watch.
eng-oncall: Watching traffic — ALB 5xx rate falling from 9% to 2% in last 2m post-dns-shift. Good sign.
maria g.: Rolling restart of the ingress controller in eu-west-2 to clear any stale KV caches: `kubectl -n ingress rollout restart deployment/ingress-controller`.
chris t.: Also reverting the small autoscaler tweak as a precaution — rolling back controller deploy from earlier today in eu-west-1 (not the root cause but want to minimize variables).
eng-oncall: Note: ALB target group health checks show flapping for many targets in AZ-b/c. Provider side notes indicate API layer upstream was overloaded by a traffic storm at 06:10 UTC. We're verifying whether a customer request pattern triggered it.
customer-success: Notifying affected customers with preliminary incident advisory. ETA TBD once we confirm stability. Marking as "partial outage" for EU region.
leo k.: Observed weird behavior with keepalive on the NGINX-sidecar; some connections not being reused -> increasing ephemeral port usage leading to resets. Proposing to turn off keepalive for now.
maria g.: Before toggling keepalive, let's validate fallback path. Can we spawn a small canary service in eu-west-2 but on different instance types to test upstream stability?
eng-oncall: Spinning up 3 t3.medium test targets behind ALB target group to see if they also reset. `kubectl apply -f canary-deploy.yaml` -> canary pods up.
eng-oncall: Canary looks stable (no immediate resets). That suggests problem is traffic/instance saturation on production target pool.
netops-bot: Provider update: fabric packet-loss affecting intra-AZ connectivity in eu-west-2. Estimated time to fix: 45-90m. Suggest continuing traffic drain from impacted AZs.
maria g.: Action item: keep AZ-b/c drained from production until provider resolves. Set autoscaling to prefer eu-west-1 and eu-central-1. Also prepare to failover persistent sessions.
eng-oncall: Implemented scale-out in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 for ingress and model-serving. Also adjusted LB healthcheck thresholds to be more permissive during the provider incident to avoid churning.
chris t.: Logging note: collected `tcpdump -w /tmp/ingress-rst-euw2.pcap` from one node and uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-incident-logs/2933334444/ingress-rst-euw2.pcap
eng-oncall: Rolling rollback of the non-critical config change from this morning completed. Deploy-bot: `deployment-bot: rollback complete to commit f34b9c3`.
eng-oncall: Monitoring customer errors via the SLO dashboard — error budget burn stabilized after weights adjusted. Current error rate at 1.1% for EU-region customers.
ashley p.: Sent initial impact email to affected customers: includes note about mitigation and that we're diverting traffic. CS will send follow-ups as we have more info.
customer-success: Customers acknowledged, asked for postmortem and root cause when available. Escalated to account team for high-touch customers.
maria g.: Next steps: 1) keep Route53 weights for 30-60m 2) continue to monitor provider ticket 3) collect metrics for postmortem 4) draft RCA once provider confirms fabric cause or we find internal issue.
leo k.: For internal follow-up: investigate ephemeral port reuse and keepalive settings on our side. If keepalive toggling helped in canary, consider temporary setting change cluster-wide.
eng-oncall: marking this thread for incident review. tagging oncall rotation: @maria g., @leo k. Postmortem owner: leo k.
netops-bot: Provider updated ticket INC-100421 -> root cause: hardware NIC firmware bug triggered under certain burst patterns. Mitigation applied on provider side, patch rollout scheduled.
maria g.: Provider says they pushed a targeted mitigation and are rolling firmware fix. We'll keep AZs drained until confirmation.
eng-oncall: Verification: after 22 minutes, ALB 5xx rate near baseline (0.4%). Reintroducing AZ traffic slowly — changing Route53 weights to 10% for eu-west-2a only.
ashley p.: weight change applied. Watching.
eng-oncall: Observing no regression for 10m while 10% traffic to eu-west-2a. Will continue stepwise.
customer-success: Updated customers: root cause appears to be provider network hardware issue; we've routed customers away and are monitoring. No data loss reported.
leo k.: Action items logged: (a) verify keepalive defaults and possibly disable for ingress (b) add conntrack alerts for AZ-level spikes (c) automate faster DNS weight-shift runbook.
maria g.: Final status: service stabilized, provider mitigation in place. Leave incident open until provider confirms firmware rollout complete. Timestamps: incident opened 2933334444, mitigation applied 2933334560, partial traffic reintroduction 2933334640.
eng-oncall: :white_check_mark: Declaring incident mitigation successful for now. Will create formal incident ticket and link this thread. Thanks all.
sre-bot: Incident summary saved to /incidents/2933334444/summary.automated.log. Please file postmortem within 72h.
eng-oncall: Closing handoff to postmortem team.
